legend.documented: a printed source in the repository supports exactly this number
legend.inferred: reasoned from documented numbers or the plan's own text
legend.plausible-procedural: a look parameter; no source; marked in the product

meta.tracers: No tracer effect exists for muskets (none in 1863). Fuse trails exist for timed-fuze shell and spherical case only (T2-203).

physical.c_sound_ms.basis: speed of sound at 20 C (PDF C.6 hypotheses: about 343 m/s); the audio mixer owns the flash-to-sound delay d/c (audio/contract/FIRE_EVENT.md section 2)

smoke.kappa_m2_per_kg.basis: mass extinction coefficient of the smoke aerosol, a look parameter in the range typical for sub-micron combustion aerosols (a few m2/g); not retrieved from a source; with it a 60-grain musket puff of sigma 0.5 m is optically thick (about 3) and a 2.5 lb gun cloud stays visible for tens of seconds

smoke.yield_frac.basis: share of the black-powder charge mass that leaves the muzzle as visible particulate; general chemistry knowledge, not retrieved; the plan gives no figure

smoke.albedo.basis: single-scattering albedo of white-grey powder smoke ("dense white-grey" cloud, audio/contract/FIRE_EVENT.md section 3)

smoke.hg_g.basis: Henyey-Greenstein forward-scattering asymmetry used for sun/moon scattering in the cloud

smoke.visible_od.basis: optical depth below which a puff no longer counts as visible (lifetime measurements)

smoke.opaque_od.basis: optical depth above which a puff hides what is behind it (sight-line hiding)

smoke.diffusion.K_h_m2s.basis: small-scale turbulent diffusivity of a young puff (grows as sigma^2 = s0^2 + 2K t + beta t^3)

smoke.diffusion.beta_h_m2s3.basis: Richardson-type growth term (slow: the cloud keeps its body); with the breeze dissipation time below, a 12-pdr cloud in the mid wind falls under the visible optical depth after 21.5 s: inside the plan G12 band (smoke plume lifetime 15 to 25 s); the same cloud in near-calm air lasts 102 s ("smoke hangs low in nearly windless heat", B.6.14.2) and a musket puff 15 s (prototype EV_LIFE 14 s)

smoke.diffusion.vertical_ratio_open.basis: vertical/horizontal diffusion ratio in open mixed air

smoke.diffusion.vertical_ratio_damp.basis: vertical/horizontal diffusion ratio in damp, stable air: smoke hangs low and spreads along the ground (T2-122: smoke pools in low ground)

smoke.dissipation_tau_s.breeze.basis: e-folding time of visible smoke mass (agglomeration, evaporation, loss of contrast) with wind at or above the reference speed; fitted with beta_h to the plan G12 plume lifetime band

smoke.dissipation_tau_s.calm.basis: same in nearly windless air: smoke hangs (PDF B.6.14.2: "smoke hangs low in nearly windless heat")

smoke.dissipation_tau_s.ref_wind_ms.basis: middle of the PDF recommended 2 to 6 mph (0.9 to 2.7 m/s); the owner has not chosen the wind scenario

smoke.buoyancy_scale.dry.basis: hot gas rise in dry air (look parameter, no source in the repository)

smoke.buoyancy_scale.damp.basis: damp air: smoke stays near the ground (ground-hugging)

projectile.case_burst_charge_oz.basis: spherical-case bursting charge of the 12-pdr: 4.5 oz, 78 balls. Two printed sources agree: Hand-book of Artillery (J. Roberts, Richmond: J. W. Randolph, 1861; Project Gutenberg #71575, text sha256 2039e805...c6086), Part IX p. 108 "Charges for Spherical Case Shot" (12-pdr column 78 balls, 4.5 oz) and Ordnance Manual 1861 (archive.org ordnancemanualfo00unit), p. 256-257, OCR lines 36420-36440 (OCR damaged: 78 balls and the token 4.5). A third reading, Instruction for Field Artillery 1863 p. 13 (OCR line 2540, 76 balls, "1-" = 1.0 oz, reading confidence low-medium), disagrees and is carried as the scenario fa1863_ocr (choices.caseBurstSource); which one is the default view is PENDING OWNER (Law cl.6). Source conflict registered as vis-fx-EG-FX-G04b

projectile.case_burst_charge_by_designat.basis: bursting charge of spherical case by pdr designation: Hand-book of Artillery (J. Roberts, Richmond: J. W. Randolph, 1861; Project Gutenberg #71575, text sha256 2039e805...c6086), Part IX p. 108 (also 18-pdr 5, 42-pdr 9, 8-in 15, not used by the effects); the transcription is Gutenberg volunteers text, not checked against page images; CORROBORATED (vis-fx round 2) by a third printed source, The Field Manual for the Use of the Officers on Ordnance Duty (Ordnance Bureau, Richmond: Ritchie & Dunnavant, 1862; archive.org fieldmanualforus00conf, OCR), printed p. 76 table Spherical Case Shot: 6-pdr 38 balls 2.5 oz, 12-pdr 78 balls 4.5 oz, 24-pdr 175 balls 6 oz, 32-pdr 225 balls 8 oz. The prose of the same manual on p. 23 says the 12-pdr case shot holds about 90 bullets and 1 oz, which agrees with the fa1863_ocr scenario and not with its own table (internal conflict, carried as the scenario)

scenario fa1863_ocr: the bursting-charge row of Instruction for Field Artillery 1863 p. 13 read from raw OCR (tokens "1-4 / 1-2 / 1- / 0-5" read as 1.4, 1.2, 1.0, 0.5 oz); page image not inspected; conflicts with the two sources above; kept as a selectable scenario, not discarded

projectile.shell_burst_charge_oz.basis: common-shell bursting charge of the 12-pdr shell, 5 oz (0 lb 5 oz "to burst the shell"): Hand-book of Artillery (J. Roberts, Richmond: J. W. Randolph, 1861; Project Gutenberg #71575, text sha256 2039e805...c6086), Part IX p. 108 "Charges for Field Shells". The table column is headed 12-pdr; applying it to the Napoleon and the 12-pdr howitzer is inferred (Instruction for Field Artillery 1863 p. 11-12: a shell is designated by the weight of the solid shot of the same diameter, and the same ammunition serves the 12-pdr and light 12-pdr guns; both have the 4.62 in. bore)

projectile.shell_burst_charge_by_designa.basis: bursting charge of common shell by pdr designation: Hand-book of Artillery (J. Roberts, Richmond: J. W. Randolph, 1861; Project Gutenberg #71575, text sha256 2039e805...c6086), Part IX p. 108 "Charges for Field Shells" (to burst: 32-pdr 0 lb 11 oz, 24-pdr 0 lb 8 oz, 12-pdr 0 lb 5 oz); also printed there: to fill the shell 1 lb 5 oz / 1 lb 0 oz / 0 lb 8 oz and service charge 1 lb 0 oz / 0 lb 12 oz / 0 lb 7 oz, which match the raw OCR of Instruction for Field Artillery 1863 p. 12 (fill and service rows readable, burst row not); CORROBORATED (vis-fx round 2) by The Field Manual for the Use of the Officers on Ordnance Duty (Richmond 1862; archive.org fieldmanualforus00conf, OCR), printed p. 76 table Charging Shells: to burst 11, 8 and 5 oz for the 32, 24 and 12-pdr, the same numbers (rows partly garbled in OCR)

projectile.shell_burst_charge_unlisted_o.basis: common-shell bursting charge of pieces whose shell is not in the printed table (6-pdr gun, mountain howitzer, every rifled gun): stand-in equal to the 12-pdr value; gap FX-G04 (rifled shells and the 6-pdr shell)

projectile.burst_sigma0_m.basis: airburst puff initial sigma (look parameter, no source in the repository)

projectile.burst_flash_ms.basis: burst flash duration (look parameter, no source in the repository)

projectile.fuze_max_s.basis: Bormann metallic time fuze graduated to 5.5 s (Instruction for Field Artillery 1863; ORD-FUZE-FA)

projectile.fuze_sparks_trail_ms.basis: fuze trail sampled sparks every 40 ms; visible only at night or dusk

projectile.fuze_trail_min_dark.basis: night weight (0 day .. 1 full night) above which fuse trails are drawn; the plan lists "fuse trails" as a night light source (T2-203, plausible-procedural)

projectile.impact_throw_speed_ms.basis: speed of the earth column: gives a 10 to 25 m column for a field-gun shell (plan G12 reference, not a measurement)

projectile.impact_dust_kg_per_kj.basis: dust mass raised per kJ of impact energy at the dry reference (a 12-pdr shot at 440 m/s carries about 540 kJ: 0.05 kg gives a column optical depth of about 3 for sigma 2 m); look parameter

projectile.clods_per_impact.basis: ballistic clod particles per ground impact

projectile.canister_spread_frac.basis: canister and grape leave the piece in a cone, most balls near the centre, "the extreme ones separating about one tenth of the range" (Gibbon, Artillerist Manual 1860, chapter Practice of fire, p. 268-269 of the printed book, OCR bub_gb_8FEkwTZd9FMC line 15629-15636; page image not inspected). Read as the full width of the pattern = 0.10 x range (the literal reading of "separating"); the statement is documented, the reading is inferred

projectile.canister_spread_frac_alt.basis: other reading of the same sentence: each extreme ball is one tenth of the range off the axis, full width 0.20 x range; carried as the alternative (choices.canisterSpread = "wide")

projectile.canister_cone_deg.basis: half-angle of the canister fan = atan(canister_spread_frac / 2) = 2.862 degrees (Gibbon 1860: extreme balls separate about one tenth of the range; the alternative reading gives 5.71 degrees). Replaces the earlier plausible-procedural stand-in of 12 degrees (gap FX-G05); PDF B.6.14.2 (27 balls inside 350 to 400 yd) gives no angle

projectile.canister_sigma_per_halfwidth.basis: lateral sigma of the ground-strike dust fan = this x half width of the pattern at the strike range (edge at 2 sigma; Gibbon says most balls are near the centre); a look parameter

projectile.canister_dust_range_m.basis: ground-strike dust fan range for canister (the PDF effective range is 350 to 400 yd)

projectile.ricochet_hops_dry.basis: solid-shot hops on dry ground (documented qualitatively: bounces and rolls on dry ground, stops in soggy earth)

projectile.ricochet_restitution.basis: hop length ratio (look parameter, no source in the repository)

projectile.ricochet_wet_stop.basis: wetness at or above which solid shot stops at the first strike ("stops in soggy earth"); threshold is ours

dust.wetness_dust_free.basis: ground wetness (0..1, environment wetness schedule) at or above which roads give no dust; the PDF only says 0.3 after the 6 pm storm of Jul 3 is "mud on roads"

dust.drying_tau_h.basis: e-folding drying time of the ground after rain; chosen so Jun 28 midday is dusty, as the PDF says "dry, dusty weather (June 28 to 30)" (inferred in the PDF: no direct dust accounts); the weather file lists the decay as a gap

dust.steps_per_min_default.basis: common time, 90 steps in a minute of 28 inches (Hardee, Rifle and Light Infantry Tactics, School of the Soldier: "the rate of ninety in a minute"; OCR hardeesrifleligh01hard, riflelightinfant121hard, infantrytacticsf01brig in tmp/library/misc). Used only when a unit_march event gives neither stepsPerMin nor a known gait

dust.gait_steps_per_min.basis: marching cadences printed by Hardee (Rifle and Light Infantry Tactics 1855, Infantry Tactics 1861): common time 90, quick time 110 ("one hundred and ten steps per minute"), route step 110 (para 306 / 311), double quick 165 ("one hundred and sixty-five steps in the minute"), double quick under urgent circumstances 180 (para 114 / 121). Verified in the OCR texts in tmp/library/misc; page images not inspected. Closes gap FX-G07 for the infantry cadence

budget.tiers.desktop.basis: plan G12 limit of 4 ms on the Arc reference (render/PLAN.md); cost factor 1 = the measured Arc numbers

budget.tiers.laptop.basis: integrated GPU sharing the frame with a 7 ms soldier budget (render/PLAN.md section 3.4)

budget.tiers.tablet.basis: tablet GPU, estimated twice the Arc cost per particle

budget.tiers.phone.basis: phone GPU, three times the Arc cost per particle (mobile_factor)

budget.class_floor.basis: every effect class keeps at least this share of the particle budget so none vanishes

budget.class_priority.basis: order in which classes are filled under a tight budget

budget.min_per_event.basis: an on-screen event keeps at least one sprite when the effects are NOT capped; under a cap sprites are shared by error-diffusion rounding and a far event may get none (its mass stays in the fog map)

budget.governor.basis: additive-increase, multiplicative-decrease on the effect scale from the measured effect cost
